title: Iberia: heat and fire

link.method: Pearson r of daily values: network mean station maximum temperature (GHCN-Daily) vs daily total fire radiative power in mainland Spain and Portugal (VIIRS), fires following the heat by 0 to 5 days
link.lag_search: lags 0..5 days, partner following the hero only (negative lag = partner leads)

gaps: Heat = daily maximum temperature at 20 NOAA GHCN-Daily weather stations in Spain and Portugal (national weather services' synoptic stations). The lane is the network mean: the mean of the normals plus the mean departure of the stations reporting that day (28 station-days missing out of 1840, none bridged; a day needs 75% of the stations).
Normal = each station's 1991 to 2020 mean for the same calendar day (+-7 days); the faint glass pillars show it at the same scale.

Fire points: all 14,856 VIIRS detections in mainland Spain and Portugal in the window, merged into 3,211 flames (detections within 2 km on the same day become one flame at their strongest detection, size = their summed FRP).

Flame size is linear in summed FRP up to 1287 MW (99th percentile); larger flames drawn at that size. Only nominal and high confidence vegetation fire detections; VIIRS passes about twice a day, and smoke or cloud can hide fires.

Smoke = GEOS-CF surface PM2.5 (a model with satellite data assimilated, not a measurement), daily mean of 8 three-hourly values, 0.25 deg; drawn linear from a floor of 8 to 60 ug/m3, higher values at full density. Particles move on GEOS-CF daily mean 10 m wind (1 deg). Part of the haze over Iberia in summer is Saharan dust, which the model also counts as PM2.5.

Afternoon heat map = GEOS-CF 2 m temperature (model), the highest of 8 three-hourly values each day at 0.5 deg, colour linear from 20 (blue) through 32 (white) to 44 deg C (red). Three-hourly samples and 50 km cells miss the hottest hour and the hottest valleys, so the map reads a few degrees cooler than the stations (day to day r = 0.99 with the station lane).
Heatwave bands = runs of at least 3 days with the network mean at least 2 sd (5.8 deg C) above its 1991 to 2020 normal (a simple rule for this story, not the official national definitions).

The link uses all 92 days; hot spells last several days and big fires burn for days, so consecutive days are not independent: r is indicative, not a test. Heat dries the vegetation over weeks and fires need ignitions and wind, so a strong same-week link is not expected.

hero_norm.method: network mean of station daily maximum temperature; normal = each station's 1991 to 2020 mean for that calendar day (+-7 days), sd = spread of the daily network anomaly over the June to August days of 1991 to 2020

sources.name: GHCN-Daily v3, daily maximum temperature (TMAX)
sources.producer: NOAA NCEI, from AEMET and IPMA synoptic stations

sources.name: VIIRS S-NPP 375 m active fires (VNP14IMG), country yearly CSV (Spain, Portugal)
GEOS-CF v1 assimilation, surface PM2.5 (pm25_rh35_gcc), 10 m wind, 2 m temperature
